summary: Zyryanka Airport (ZKP/UESU) is a medium-sized regional airport serving the remote settlement of Zyryanka in the Sakha Republic (Yakutia), Russian Far East. It functions as a critical transportation lifeline for this isolated community in one of the coldest inhabited regions on Earth. The airport primarily handles regional flights connecting residents to Yakutsk and other Siberian hubs.
faqs:
Q: Where is Zyryanka Airport located?
A: Zyryanka Airport is located near the settlement of Zyryanka in the Sakha Republic (Yakutia) in the Russian Far East, at approximately 65.7°N latitude.

Q: What is Zyryanka Airport primarily used for?
A: The airport serves as the main air link for the remote Zyryanka community, providing passenger transport, mail delivery, and cargo services that are essential due to the lack of year-round road connectivity.

Q: When is the best time to fly to Zyryanka?
A: Summer months (June through August) offer the most reliable weather conditions, as the region experiences extreme winter cold with temperatures regularly dropping below -40°C (-40°F).

Q: Are there regular commercial flights to Zyryanka?
A: Regional carriers operate scheduled flights, typically connecting Zyryanka with Yakutsk, though schedules and frequencies can vary by season.
transport_tips: There is no rail service to Zyryanka, and road access is extremely limited, especially during winter freeze-up and spring thaw periods when rivers become impassable. Travelers typically rely on the airport or seasonal river transport along the Kolyma River. Taxis and informal transport are available in the small settlement for getting to and from the terminal.
local_tip: Pack for extreme cold even in shoulder seasons—temperatures can drop sharply from October through May, and layered clothing is essential as airport facilities offer limited indoor waiting areas.
